ca-alameda-2026-boe2-lieber-sally.name: Sally J. Lieber
ca-alameda-2026-boe2-lieber-sally.bio: Chair of the State Board of Equalization; former city councilmember, mayor, county commissioner, State Assemblymember, and Franchise Tax Board member.

positions.stance: Says state agencies must be transparent and accountable, enhancing available information and making it accessible and usable; is running a corporate-free campaign.
Wants the Board of Equalization fully staffed with highly trained personnel and future staff recruited through colleges and universities.
Will continue examining affordable-housing funding programs, ensure voter-approved housing funds are used wisely, and keep state tax credits "transparent, sustainable and fair."
Calls the climate crisis "an existential threat for California" and wants every government agency working toward sustainability, including greenbelt protection.
Commits to serving veterans, homeowners, seniors, people with disabilities, and small businesses through housing, services, and access to information.

ca-alameda-2026-boe2-pimentel-john.name: John Pimentel
ca-alameda-2026-boe2-pimentel-john.bio: Former California Deputy Secretary for Transportation, community college trustee, and Menlo Park housing commissioner; clean energy and water infrastructure developer.

positions.stance: "End the sales tax on food," which he calls a regressive tax that burdens working families, seniors, and young people.
Close tax loopholes so large corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share, naming the Water's Edge Election, Invest/Borrow/Die, and carried interest.
Strengthen transparency and accountability so the Board of Equalization operates effectively and earns the public's trust.

tx-denton-2026-county-clerk-frey-dale.name: Dale Frey
tx-denton-2026-county-clerk-frey-dale.bio: Former web developer and systems administrator supporting federal agencies including GSA, the U.S. Geological Survey and NOAA; previously ran for Texas State Senate District 30.

positions.stance: Promises to "serve all Denton County residents professionally, respectfully, and according to the law," including issuing marriage licenses.
Supports countywide Election Day voting centers so voters can cast a ballot at any open polling place in the county.
Says if documentary proof-of-citizenship rules are imposed, the public should socialize the cost of passports so no eligible voter is priced out.
Says Denton County should advocate against 287(g) ICE integration because local public safety depends on trust.

tx-fort-bend-2026-da-mcdonald-shawn.name: Shawn McDonald
tx-fort-bend-2026-da-mcdonald-shawn.bio: Board-certified criminal lawyer and former Henderson County felony prosecutor with more than twenty-five years in Texas courtrooms.

positions.stance: Says he answers "to Fort Bend County families - not to George Soros or any outside special interests."
Aggressively prosecute murderers, rapists, armed robbers and gang members; "No more unbridled diversion offers" or widespread dismissals and lenient deals.
Prosecute crimes against children, the elderly and vulnerable victims "with maximum effectiveness and appropriate punishment."
Stand with law enforcement and strengthen partnerships with police, deputies and investigators rather than creating divisions to police them.
Wants to "End Outsourced Justice" and restore local control, saying he is not running to implement a national political agenda.

tx-fort-bend-2026-da-middleton-brian.name: Brian M Middleton
tx-fort-bend-2026-da-middleton-brian.bio: Fort Bend County District Attorney since 2019 and certified Texas peace officer; 2022 Texas Prosecutor of the Year.

positions.stance: "Tough on violent crime"; coordinates multi-agency operations to take violent offenders, fugitives and human traffickers off the streets.
Expanded protections for family-violence victims, prosecuted abusers, and partnered with nonprofits and shelters serving women and children.
Created the county's first Civil Rights and Public Integrity Divisions to institutionalize accountability for those in positions of public trust.
Running "to bring business discipline to public service — to modernize systems, train staff, and measure results."

tx-fort-bend-2026-county-clerk-mcfarlane.name: Tamara McFarlane
tx-fort-bend-2026-county-clerk-mcfarlane.bio: Small-business owner in real estate, former land acquisitions leader and government auditor, and former Fort Bend County Election Judge.

positions.stance: Will ensure "every dollar is spent wisely" and every office runs with transparency and efficiency, keeping government small and accountable.
Will fight to ensure "every legal vote is counted, every illegal vote is rejected," and elections remain transparent and secure.
Pledges to uphold "faith, family, and freedom" and conservative principles that keep government accountable.
Proposes measurable service standards, published wait times, workload forecasting and online queue management as the county grows.
Plans a line-by-line operational review, public performance dashboard, cost-per-transaction reporting and an annual taxpayer-facing performance report.

tx-fort-bend-2026-county-clerk-jones-son.name: Sonya Jones
tx-fort-bend-2026-county-clerk-jones-son.bio: Former Fort Bend ISD trustee, Houston ISD math and science teacher, and university academic advisor.

positions.stance: Maintain "the highest standards in record protection" and support for the Commissioners Court.
Expand language-accessible and online services so every resident can engage with the county clerk's office.
Guarantee "an open book and open-door policy for records."
Streamline services, reduce wait times, and use smart technology to modernize the clerk's office.
Partner with local agencies and organizations and safeguard records to strengthen Fort Bend's future.

tx-fort-bend-2026-treasurer-rickert-bill.name: Bill Rickert
tx-fort-bend-2026-treasurer-rickert-bill.bio: Fort Bend County Treasurer since his 2018 election; former Petroleum Geo-Services vice president.

tx-fort-bend-2026-treasurer-boney-jeffre.name: Jeffrey L Boney
tx-fort-bend-2026-treasurer-boney-jeffre.bio: Founder and CEO of the Texas Business Alliance; former president and CEO of the Greater Houston Black Chamber and Washington Mutual Bank employee.

positions.stance: Treat every taxpayer dollar "as if it came from my own family's wallet," spending wisely and reducing waste.
Operate county government with full transparency so residents know how tax dollars are used, with services reaching all neighborhoods.
Create new pathways for meaningful public input so residents have a say in decisions affecting their daily lives.

tx-montgomery-2026-da-holley-mike.name: Mike Holley
tx-montgomery-2026-da-holley-mike.bio: Montgomery County District Attorney appointed by the governor; former First Assistant DA, Army JAG officer, defense attorney and law professor.

positions.stance: Supports "strong, lawful sentences" for violent offenders, sexual predators and repeat serious offenders.
Victims deserve to be heard, kept informed and treated with respect, "regardless of money, connections, or political views."
Will examine evidence fairly, meet disclosure obligations, and work to clear people the evidence shows are innocent.
Prosecutors should answer officers' calls, help build sound cases and arrive prepared, with honest feedback and accountability.
Recruit talented prosecutors, investigators and staff, provide training and mentors, and deliver efficient work for taxpayers.

tx-montgomery-2026-county-clerk-steinman.name: Brandon Steinmann
tx-montgomery-2026-county-clerk-steinman.bio: District director for U.S. Rep. Kevin Brady and former director of State-Federal Relations for Gov. Rick Perry.

positions.stance: Continue modernizing the office so more documents and tasks are available online rather than requiring an office visit.
"Remove COVID barriers and screening to make the office more accessible and comfortable for the public."
Create a social media presence to guide the public through County Clerk tasks and filings.
Streamline office operations, eliminate redundant work, and review best practices from similarly sized counties.

tx-tarrant-2026-cda-sorrells-phil.name: Phil Sorrells
tx-tarrant-2026-cda-sorrells-phil.bio: Tarrant County Criminal District Attorney since 2023; former Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 10 judge for 25 years and assistant criminal district attorney.

tx-tarrant-2026-cda-burks-tiffany.name: Tiffany Burks
tx-tarrant-2026-cda-burks-tiffany.bio: Partner and criminal division lead at Varghese Summersett; former Fort Bend and Tarrant County prosecutor who rose to deputy chief of the criminal division.

positions.stance: Will prosecute violent and predatory crime aggressively while upholding "the constitutional rights every citizen is guaranteed."
The DA's office should give the county sound legal advice to prevent costly civil lawsuits and mismanagement of public funds.
Will expand proven diversion programs that hold youth accountable while giving them "a genuine path to turn their lives around."
Will prioritize partnerships addressing root causes of crime — homelessness, mental illness, addiction — and collaboration with law enforcement.
Committed to properly investigating deaths in the Tarrant County jail system: "accountability in custody is not optional."
